approach.method_basis: The Parent trains a recurrent SMILES language model on an unlabeled molecular corpus and starts each objective with a fresh policy copied from that frozen prior. Each accepted batch supplies its highest-scoring half, joined by the strongest eligible earlier elites from a memory of thirty-two accepted molecules. Historical examples keep their original strings and scores and receive diminishing weights according to earlier fitting exposure, with the total current and historical coefficient shares preserved. The policy fits squared error toward frozen-prior sequence log likelihood plus sixty times accepted reward, with each positive target independently capped at zero. It takes the inherited clipped Adam updates and retains the final policy. Complete SMILES are then sampled directly from that policy, and the first chemically valid, canonically novel draws fill the announced batch. Extra valid novel draws from those same calls are discarded.
approach.novelty: Add a quota of one emitted molecule per ring scaffold within each existing sampling call. The first eligible member of a scaffold is admitted in sample order; later members in that call are skipped. A refill starts a fresh allowance, so a productive scaffold can still contribute again without a global diversity ban. This moves core allocation to the point where freshly generated molecules actually reach evaluation. The earlier sibling diversified retained historical memory, where most protected alternatives never reached a later fitting update and the mean gain missed the meaningful threshold. Other siblings changed the prior or learning rule. None tested a quota on the direct emitted stream. This experiment keeps the current strong replay and target-ceiling stack and measures which sampled core alternatives gain emission. The Parent also improved through peripheral analogues, so losing productive local substitutions is a concrete risk; more core names alone will not establish useful search.

hypothesis: Within each existing direct-policy sampling call, admit at most the first valid canonically novel molecule for each successfully extracted nonempty atom/bond-typed nonisomeric Murcko scaffold, resetting the scaffold allowance at the next refill call and leaving acyclic or extraction-fallback identities under inherited admission.

finding_summary.headline: The quota broadened evaluated scaffold coverage but lowered final scores despite earlier progress.
finding_summary.insights:
This resolves the earlier uncertainty about whether protected alternatives ever reach useful downstream opportunities. Here, all 264 locally added families were scored, and 111 of their molecules entered fitting, making 212 training appearances, including 101 historical replay appearances. Direct admission therefore carried diversification through evaluation and learning. That propagation was insufficient for a final-score benefit. The 337 calls without a quota opportunity reproduced their local no-quota choices exactly, and paired behavior agreed through the first intervention in every session, narrowing the change to admission and the subsequent feedback it altered.

The result supports a tradeoff between early progress and later refinement. The parent obtained fifteen actual incumbent gains from repeated-core analogues, while the child gained only six incumbents from its locally added families. These are observations from separate completed trajectories, so they cannot price the child’s unscored rejected molecules or establish that those particular rejections caused the endpoint loss. The chemical assessment helps explain why counting cores is insufficient: productive attachment positions and combinations of peripheral groups remained uneven despite broader ring coverage. The number of evaluated molecules with potential tetrahedral centres rose from 846 to 1,145, with no assigned configurations in either cohort; the quota supplied neither configuration control nor a guarantee of preserving useful functional roles.

The open question is whether broader early coverage can coexist with sufficient sampling of productive peripheral analogues to retain late improvements. The AUC gain makes that distinction worth testing, while the lower final score rules out treating increased family coverage alone as evidence of better search.
finding_summary.results:
The admission mechanism executed correctly in all 497 sampling calls. It rejected 459 otherwise novel repeat-core draws before capacity and produced no repeated ring core within a call; the parent emitted 460 such repetitions. Against equal-sized choices from the same actual draws, 154 calls gained a total of 264 family slots: 259 ring-core appearances and five acyclic singleton appearances. Every added family reached evaluation, and six of those molecules improved the incumbent. Across complete runs, distinct evaluated ring cores increased from 2,813 to 3,079, while the largest occupancy of one core in a session fell from 160 molecules to 44. Total strict incumbent improvements nevertheless fell from 149 to 120.

The three-seed mean final score decreased from 0.522705 to 0.508379, a paired change of −0.014326 against the required +0.002 benefit. Seed changes were +0.002392, −0.018880 and −0.026492. All five task means declined, although the DRD2 endpoint difference was only about two millionths near the score ceiling. Recorded mean AUC increased from 0.405593 to 0.427858; about 94% of that aggregate increase came from DRD2, mainly its much earlier progress in seed 2. All fifteen sessions completed their budgets. Batches needing refills increased from 16 to 33, and measured generation time increased from 24.75 to 37.02 seconds. The utility falsifier is triggered; the verified admission mechanism remains confirmed.

molecular.headline: Broad, ring-rich medicinal chemistry; productive attachment patterns and stereochemical definition remain uneven.
molecular.overall_character: All five supplied tasks and all three seeds were read, including the Parent trajectories. Each task contains 900 evaluated records, of which 870 are optimizer proposals. Passive RDKit inspection of the 4,350 Child proposals finds 4,350 parseable, single-component molecules, 4,303 containing rings and 4,199 containing aromatic rings. The typical proposal has 26 heavy atoms and three perceived rings. The digest's ring-closure rates are 0.9828–0.9943 and aromatic-marker rates are 0.9391–0.992; these are fractions of SMILES containing markers, not fractions of atoms. Aromatic amides, sulfonamides, fused nitrogen heterocycles, arylpiperazines and arylpiperidines are well represented. Most recognizable small-molecule families are plausibly makeable, while the tails include simple inorganic species, oversized polyaromatics or peptides, and unusual nitrogen functionality. Drug-likeness is moderate because plausible medicinal frameworks coexist with substantial size, flexibility and substitution liabilities; no synthesis route or experimental property was established. Structural breadth is real: the evaluated proposals contain 3,079 distinct atom/bond-typed nonisomeric Murcko ring scaffolds versus 2,813 in the Parent. Functional roles and productive substitution patterns remain much more specific than these scaffold counts. RDKit identifies potential tetrahedral centres in 1,145 Child proposals, versus 846 Parent proposals, with zero assigned centres in either; all task digest stereocentre-marker rates are also zero. This is missing configuration coverage, not evidence that a particular stereoisomer would score better. Counts retain repeated identities across seeds. Reproducible passive descriptors, input hashes and recorded-score comparisons are saved in r0012-05-improve-L03-molecular.audit.py and r0012-05-improve-L03-molecular.audit.json beside this report.

per_task.generated_character: The 870 proposals have a median of 24 heavy atoms, three rings and three aromatic rings. They are chiefly aromatic amides: acetamido benzodiazines, benzimidazole-containing systems, lactams, benzylamides and diaryl ether carboxamides carrying amidines. The leading acetamido benzodiazine/phenethyl structures have 22 heavy atoms and three aromatic rings, with ordinary amide and carbon–carbon attachment chemistry that looks synthetically plausible. Other proposals extend into large peptides and densely fused polycycles. Evaluated ring-core diversity is 604 versus the Parent's 539, while the recognizable high-scoring chemical vocabulary remains aromatic carbonyl/nitrogen chemistry.
liabilities: Large peptide extensions and highly substituted polyaromatics impose much greater size or conformational burden than the leading compact amides; extra amide or ring content alone does not retain the observed score.
Amidines change ionization and hydrogen-bonding character relative to neutral aromatic amides. Their presence is not equivalent to retaining the same nitrogen functionality.
The saturated and polycyclic tail includes unresolved tetrahedral configurations: 178 proposals contain potential tetrahedral centres and none are assigned.
missing_features: Consistent assembly of the compact aromatic amide environment is missing from many proposals: heteroarenes and carbonyls are available, but the useful combination of size, attachment position and nitrogen role is often lost during elaboration.

The leading benzodiazine positional variants do not reveal a productive direction beyond their shared score. The stronger pyridyl ether/carboxamide combinations observed in the Parent are absent from the Child's leading examples.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial indole carboxanilide scores 0.3051048083696145; four acetamido benzodiazine positional variants reach the same 0.4428306005333078. The upper recorded-score quartile occupies 20–29 heavy atoms, whereas the lower quartile spans 1–49. A fluorine-only molecule scores 0.0 and the cited 44-heavy-atom peptide extension scores 6.353312339014414e-28. Among final proposals, the amidinoaryl pyrrolidine amide scores 0.3173316605218366, but adding another aryl carboxamide gives 0.0004762091843102436. These observations favor a bounded combination of aromatic extent, nitrogen placement and carbonyl attachment, rather than monotonic elaboration. The Parent's seed-2 pyridyl ether carboxanilide at evaluation 271 scores 0.5, whereas the Child's amidine-bearing diaryl ether example reaches 0.42749549733373915; the Child seed-0 best improves on the Parent's 0.43351949803907636. The chemistry changes are uneven across seeds, and the examples do not identify a unique missing target structure.

per_task.generated_character: The proposals are especially aromatic and halogen-rich: medians are 31 heavy atoms, four rings and four aromatic rings, and the digest halogen-marker rate is 0.8747. The leading family is methoxy-substituted anilino quinazoline chemistry with a phenyl, furyl or thienyl appendage and fluorinated aniline. The best example has 27 heavy atoms and four aromatic rings; its exocyclic NH, ring nitrogen acceptors and ether are recognizable, synthetically plausible medicinal chemistry. The full trajectories also contain hydrazone-rich and other nitrogen-heteroaromatic families, polyaryl ethers and sulfones. Observed ring cores number 505 versus 355 in the Parent, but all twelve digest-best entries remain close relatives of the anilino fused-diazine family.
liabilities: Extensive aromatic surface and repeated halogenation create a plausible solubility burden; neither adding fluorine nor adding more aromatic rings consistently improves the recorded score.
The lower tail includes an activated alkene flanked by sulfonyl and ester functionality, which deserves a different reactivity reading from the stable aromatic ether examples.
Simple inorganic or very small nitrogen-containing proposals are chemically valid species but poor evidence of useful molecular construction for this observed family.
missing_features: The strongest Child family lacks the coordinated alkoxy decoration of the stronger Parent example. The missing evidence concerns successful combinations and positions of appendages, rather than access to aromatic rings, fluorine or ether groups individually.

The digest-best set contains no comparably successful alternative arrangement of the anilino donor and heteroaromatic acceptors outside this close fused-diazine family. The observed gradient provides no basis for prescribing extra saturation or basic amines.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The difluoroanilino phenylquinazoline scores 0.6460611381594701, and its trifluoro analogue scores 0.6456917428325912. Furyl and thienyl replacements each score 0.6439546794971287; these substitutions mostly preserve the local plateau. A four-aromatic-ring polyaryl ether/methylsulfone scores only 0.30122048819527814, showing that aromatic ring count alone does not explain the ordering. The vinylsulfone/unsaturated-ester example scores 0.2948214550303749, while even nitrate receives 0.5004402958788305, so a middle-range numerical value does not establish a coherent organic framework. The Parent's seed-2 evaluation-273 best is a more extensively alkoxy-decorated anilino phenylquinazoline at 0.6669492630755185. The Child preserves the general core but does not reproduce that higher-scoring peripheral arrangement among its best molecules.

per_task.generated_character: The proposals combine saturated amine rings with aromatic groups: median size is 27 heavy atoms, with four rings and two aromatic rings. The leading 24-heavy-atom arylalkyl piperidine and 29-heavy-atom arylpiperazine contain a neutral, structurally basic aliphatic nitrogen connected to hydrophobic aromatic regions. Other strong examples combine piperazines or benzazepines with phenols, methoxy groups, aniline, fluorinated heteroarenes and flexible alkyl linkers. These simple cyclic-amine families look conventionally makeable. Seed-2 later proposals also explore fused and bridged phenolic polycycles with greater configurational complexity. The Parent already generated strong arylpiperazines, benzazepine-linked amines and amino ketones; cyclic basic nitrogen is established chemistry in both cohorts.
liabilities: Several near-ceiling molecules have long flexible linkers and substantial hydrophobic aromatic surface. Their recorded scores do not resolve conformational, solubility or selectivity liabilities.

The fused and bridged phenolic alternatives can contain multiple unresolved stereocentres, making their synthetic and conformational interpretation less definite than the simple piperidine or piperazine examples.
Sulfonylation, acylation and direct aromatic attachment change nitrogen basicity. A low charged-SMILES rate does not mean the high-scoring neutral representations lack protonatable amines.
missing_features: No absent objective-required ring or amine motif is demonstrated: the highest-scoring proposals already contain the strongly associated cyclic aliphatic nitrogen and aromatic groups.

Configurational definition is missing from the complex saturated alternatives. There are 420 proposals with potential tetrahedral centres and zero assigned centres; the present scores do not establish whether stereochemical control would improve this objective.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The leading arylalkyl piperidine scores 0.9999999478348883, and the arylpiperazine scores 0.9999999026461167. All 218 upper-quartile proposals match the passive neutral amine heuristic requiring saturated carbon neighbours, compared with 15 of 218 lower-quartile proposals; this is a structural classification, not a pKa calculation. The cited sulfonylated piperidine/heteroaryl amide scores 1.9828327575562915e-05: having the ring nitrogen present is insufficient when it is incorporated into a sulfonamide. The nitro/carboxylic-acid heteroarene scores 1.8588450134335675e-05. The association is not an absolute requirement: a late nitrogen-free phenolic polycycle scores 0.6250165349329656. Both Parent and Child best examples already approach the observed numerical ceiling, so these records do not establish another objective-required pharmacophore as missing.

per_task.generated_character: The typical proposal has 23 heavy atoms, three rings and two aromatic rings. The strongest recurring chemistry is arylsulfonyl piperazine: naphthalene or indole on the sulfonyl side, with methyl, propyl, aryl, acyl or another sulfonyl group at the opposite nitrogen. The leading N-methyl naphthalenesulfonyl piperazine has 20 heavy atoms and three rings. Benzodioxane-related arylsulfonyl compounds and bis-sulfonyl piperazines add oxygenated ring environments. These motifs have familiar, plausible assembly chemistry. Broader trajectories include ordinary amides and heterocycles as well as very small acyclic species. The Child has 745 observed ring cores versus 732 in the Parent.
liabilities: Acylation or sulfonylation at the opposite nitrogen changes the molecule's ionization and hydrogen-bonding pattern. These forms should not be treated as equivalent cyclic amines.
The low tail includes an organic azide and an N-hydroxy trichloromethyl formamide, chemically unusual contexts compared with the leading arylsulfonyl series.

Multiple sulfonyl groups can add substantial polarity and mass, while small underdecorated heterocycles lose much of the aromatic attachment context; neither extreme is a reliable stand-in for the stronger combination.
missing_features: Successful joint control of aryl attachment position and opposite-nitrogen substitution remains incomplete. Piperazine and sulfonamide availability is already clear, but closely related local environments carry distinct scores.

The stronger Parent combination of heteroaryl and oxygenated aryl groups on a bis-sulfonyl piperazine is absent from the leading Child entries, although other bis-sulfonyl piperazines are generated. A universal preference for leaving one nitrogen basic is not supported.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The leading naphthalenesulfonyl piperazine scores 0.23735633163877068; relocating the naphthalene attachment gives 0.22138416879776573 with the same heavy-atom and ring counts. Replacing the opposite N-methyl substituent with propyl gives 0.20874143036171652, while an N-acyl analogue gives 0.20421640473731204. Sulfonamides occur in 131 of 218 upper-quartile proposals and 9 of 218 lower-quartile proposals. Small urea scores 0.008404548427654986 and allyl azide scores 0.0. The Parent's seed-2 evaluation-280 heteroaryl/benzodioxole bis-sulfonyl piperazine scores 0.2588686674995393, above the Child's leading simpler monosulfonyl example. Thus the observed preference concerns assembled aromatic/sulfonyl/nitrogen environments, not merely a free basic nitrogen or any sulfur-containing molecule.

per_task.generated_character: This is chemically heterogeneous output with median size 24 heavy atoms, three rings and two aromatic rings. The leading 26-heavy-atom molecule is a branched, fluorinated anilide/oxamide containing three amide linkages and one aromatic ring; its branched centre has no assigned configuration and its nitrogens are amidic, not a free aliphatic amine. Another strong 25-heavy-atom molecule combines a methyl benzoate, arylsulfonyl group and aryl-substituted cyclic amidine. A separate 20-heavy-atom example has a guanidine-substituted, phenyl-bearing partially saturated fused ring system. Other candidates carry nitrogen heterocycles, thioamides, esters and guanidines. These are recognizable but chemically distinct families, with more demanding or ambiguous synthesis in the complex polycyclic and peptide tail. Observed ring cores number 780 versus the Parent's 774.
liabilities: Oversized polyaromatics, lipid-like chains and peptide elaborations add extensive size or flexibility and occur among the zero-score examples.

The leading branched compound masks its nitrogen functionality as amides, while other strong examples use cyclic amidines or guanidines. These represent different ionization tendencies and donor/acceptor arrangements, rather than interchangeable nitrogen counts.
Later proposals can retain fluorinated aromatics, carbonyls and heterocyclic nitrogens yet score very poorly; these isolated motifs are insufficient evidence of the useful complete molecular context.
missing_features: Repeated production of compact molecules with a successful joint carbonyl, nitrogen and sulfonyl arrangement is missing from much of the later output. These groups are individually plentiful, while their location and chemical role vary substantially.

The branched leading anilide and the guanidine-bearing fused-ring example lack stereochemical definition. In total, 290 proposals have potential tetrahedral centres and none are assigned; objective benefit from assigning them remains unmeasured.

The strongest Parent's compact arylsulfonyl/acetylamine arrangement is absent from the Child's leading examples. The records do not justify replacing this observed assembly gap with a prescribed benchmark-specific fragment.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The branched anilide/oxamide scores 0.3085499097640706, the sulfonyl cyclic-amidine ester 0.3034617343186778, and the guanidine-containing fused-ring example 0.2711448282680827. The upper recorded-score quartile has a median of 22 heavy atoms versus 31 in the lower quartile; the cited 63-heavy-atom polyaryl molecule, long-chain lipid-like molecule and peptide all score 0.0. Size alone is insufficient: the final 24-heavy-atom heterocyclic carboxylic acid/amide scores 7.082584041248927e-09. Adding fluorines to the strong sulfonyl cyclic-amidine ester gives 0.18136420222115457. The Parent's seed-2 evaluation-291 best, a compact fluorinated arylsulfonyl/acetylamine arrangement, scores 0.32609684308650033; both cohorts share the Child's evaluation-87 best molecule at 0.3085499097640706. The evidence favors particular compact polar arrangements, but cannot establish one required fluorinated ring, free-amine motif or target-like scaffold from these chemically different winners.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The cited naphthalenesulfonyl positional isomers have identical heavy-atom and ring counts but scores 0.23735633163877068 and 0.22138416879776573. Additional fluorination of a cited sulfonyl cyclic-amidine ester changes 0.3034617343186778 to 0.18136420222115457. Free cyclic aliphatic amines characterize one high-scoring cohort, while arylsulfonyl nitrogen and largely nonbasic aromatic systems characterize others. Evaluated ring-scaffold breadth already exceeds the Parent's, so missing rings or a universal missing basic amine would misdescribe the output.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator reaches many frameworks but does not reliably reproduce the local attachment patterns that distinguish useful complete molecules.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A task-agnostic generator needs chemically distinguishable choices for attachment position, bond order, carbonyl or sulfonyl connectivity, and nitrogen conjugation while changing a framework or appendage. It should retain access to both basic and nonbasic nitrogen environments and let accepted molecular feedback determine which combinations to reproduce, without a fixed preferred ring or functional group.

transferable_gaps.evidence: A cited amidinoaryl amide scores 0.3173316605218366, while its more extensively aryl-amide-decorated relative scores 0.0004762091843102436. A compact 26-heavy-atom branched anilide/oxamide scores 0.3085499097640706, while a 63-heavy-atom polyaryl example and a long-chain lipid-like example score 0.0. At the opposite extreme, fluorine-only and small urea proposals provide little assembled organic context. Other high-scoring molecules retain longer aromatic-alkyl amine architectures, so the observations do not support one universal size optimum.
transferable_gaps.gap: The output does not show reliable control of complete-molecule size and polar-group assembly during elaboration.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: The generator should support controlled additions, removals and rearrangements of appendages while maintaining a coherent full molecular context. Joint size, flexibility and polar-group combinations need to remain learnable from supplied scalar feedback; blanket shortening, a shared atom-count cutoff or indiscriminate heteroatom addition would erase distinctions visible in these trajectories.

transferable_gaps.evidence: All five digest stereocentre-marker rates are 0.0. Passive RDKit perception identifies potential tetrahedral centres in 1,145 of 4,350 Child proposals, comprising 1,950 centres, with zero assigned centres; the Parent also has zero assigned centres. The cited branched anilide/oxamide, guanidine-bearing fused-ring molecule and complex phenolic polycycles demonstrate that the absence is not explained by entirely achiral output.
transferable_gaps.gap: Explicit tetrahedral configuration is absent even when the generator produces constitutionally stereogenic molecules.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A task-agnostic molecular representation and generation process would need to express and preserve eligible configurations and keep distinct stereoisomer identities distinguishable. This is a concrete missing chemical capability; whether using it helps must be learned or measured through ordinary feedback, without selecting a preferred configuration from hidden task identity.

method_name: Augmented Hill-Climb with a corpus-trained SMILES policy
method_thesis: Train a compact autoregressive SMILES prior solely on the supplied unlabeled corpus, then initialize a fresh policy from that prior for each objective. Use the initial observations and each subsequent scored batch to update only its highest-reward sequences with the Augmented Hill-Climb loss: fit policy log likelihood to frozen-prior log likelihood plus scaled observed reward. Sample complete molecules token by token from the updated policy, canonicalize them, and refill invalid or duplicate proposals by further generation. The corpus supplies language training, never a ranked molecular pool. Elite-conditioned policy updates should shift generation toward new high-scoring molecular combinations quickly enough to improve the benchmark's mean final Top-1. This is a small-budget transfer hypothesis, not a claim that published larger-budget gains carry over. The root uses the current scored batch; randomized historical replay is reserved for the first improvement. The anchor's elite augmented-likelihood mechanism is described by [Thomas et al.](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s13321-022-00646-z).

activation_observables.measurement: Join every emitted canonical identity to its actual generation call, sample row, sampled token IDs, EOS status, policy-feedback version and exact raw SMILES. Re-decode tokens and re-canonicalize the raw string; both must reproduce its pending accepted-score serialization and canonical/isomeric identity. Verify increasing sample-row order within calls, original seen/batch_seen exclusions, unchanged conditional multinomial sampling and no diagnostic RNG consumption. On matched inputs before the first admission intervention, the raw and emitted prefixes must match the Parent. Later changed feedback is allowed, but no graph edit, substitute library molecule, raw-string repair or diagnostic-only record may become an emitted candidate.
activation_observables.name: Trace emitted identities to actual sampled tokens, completion status, generation call, sample row and policy-update version; verify pending raw strings and canonical accepted identities agree.

activation_observables.measurement: Reconstruct every call from its raw-row receipts and starting still-needed count. The first eligible nonempty scaffold key can emit, any later otherwise-admissible occurrence of that key in the same call before capacity must be quota-rejected, and the allowance must reset on the next call. Require zero within-call repeated emitted ring-scaffold keys. Count actual quota opportunities separately from already-full capacity discards, invalidity, incompletion and identity duplicates. Verify the exact novel=emitted+quota-rejected+capacity-discarded partition, and retain valid, novel and termination denominators. Report generation calls, batches requiring refills, acyclic/extraction-fallback opportunities, total measured runtime and bounded failures. Compare call-local actual output with the passive no-quota choice on the same raw draws; if no potential duplicate-core admission occurs before capacity, the call is a local control. There is no preregistered promise that raw validity or identity-duplicate rate improves.
activation_observables.name: Measure raw sequence termination, RDKit validity, identity duplicates, valid novel surplus, capacity discards, refill calls and actual runtime separately; emitted batch size alone cannot estimate raw generation quality.

activation_observables.measurement: Compute the specified atom/bond-typed nonisomeric Murcko keys independently for all recorded raw valid draws and emitted identities. At each actual call compare family coverage against the first k valid novel no-quota candidates, with k equal to the actual emitted count; use ring-scaffold keys and canonical singleton keys for acyclic/fallback identities, reporting those categories separately. Register a positive summed actual-minus-comparator distinct-family count on opportunities where the first k comparator candidates repeat a ring scaffold, and require that the extra families are actual emitted identities, not only rejected or surplus draws. Also report the full R-sized comparator and any actual shortfall before refill. Across batches and sessions report ring-core counts, concentration, duplicate-core positions and core-quota replacements; cores may repeat across calls, so session-wide diversity is measured rather than guaranteed. Join molecular sizes, appendage/polar-group descriptors and eligible/assigned stereochemistry descriptively to these cohorts without adding any admission criterion or claiming that a Murcko key preserves functional role or configuration.

approach.method_basis: The Parent trains a recurrent SMILES language model on an unlabeled molecular corpus and starts each objective with a fresh policy copied from that frozen prior. Each accepted batch supplies its highest-scoring half, joined by the strongest eligible earlier elites from a memory of thirty-two accepted molecules. Historical examples keep their original strings and scores and receive diminishing weights according to earlier fitting exposure, with the total current and historical coefficient shares preserved. The policy fits squared error toward frozen-prior sequence log likelihood plus sixty times accepted reward, with each positive target independently capped at zero. It takes the inherited clipped Adam updates and retains the final policy. Complete SMILES are then sampled directly from that policy, and the first chemically valid, canonically novel draws fill the announced batch. Extra valid novel draws from those same calls are discarded.
approach.novelty: Add a quota of one emitted molecule per ring scaffold within each existing sampling call. The first eligible member of a scaffold is admitted in sample order; later members in that call are skipped. A refill starts a fresh allowance, so a productive scaffold can still contribute again without a global diversity ban. This moves core allocation to the point where freshly generated molecules actually reach evaluation. The earlier sibling diversified retained historical memory, where most protected alternatives never reached a later fitting update and the mean gain missed the meaningful threshold. Other siblings changed the prior or learning rule. None tested a quota on the direct emitted stream. This experiment keeps the current strong replay and target-ceiling stack and measures which sampled core alternatives gain emission. The Parent also improved through peripheral analogues, so losing productive local substitutions is a concrete risk; more core names alone will not establish useful search.

research_intent.falsifier: The admission mechanism is refuted if two successfully extracted identical nonempty ring-scaffold keys are emitted in one generation call, if a later eligible occurrence before capacity is admitted despite an earlier same-key emission, if a first eligible core is rejected solely by this quota, or if the allowance persists into the next call. Grouping all acyclic molecules together, changing canonical/isomeric identity, emitting a saved or edited molecule, or introducing an unrelated chemical or score threshold violates the bound mechanism. If repeat-core opportunities occur but neither actual emitted identities nor conditional equal-count family coverage changes on any qualifying call, the claim that the gate moves emitted support is unsupported; no opportunities leaves it untested. A core extraction failure must follow the declared original-admission fallback and be counted rather than hidden. The first-k same-draw comparator must use identical initial exclusions and recorded raw draws without extra randomness or labels. Inconsistent novelty accounting, changed learned weights on identical feedback, altered upstream memory/loss rules or unbounded refill violates isolation. Increased core coverage with a paired mean benefit below the supplied threshold, or incomplete generation that prevents a complete paired comparison, rejects utility without undoing verified quota activation. Loss of productive analogues, unchanged session-wide core counts and repeats across separate refill calls do not themselves refute the call-local mechanism.

finding_summary.headline: The quota broadened evaluated scaffold coverage but lowered final scores despite earlier progress.
finding_summary.insights:
This resolves the earlier uncertainty about whether protected alternatives ever reach useful downstream opportunities. Here, all 264 locally added families were scored, and 111 of their molecules entered fitting, making 212 training appearances, including 101 historical replay appearances. Direct admission therefore carried diversification through evaluation and learning. That propagation was insufficient for a final-score benefit. The 337 calls without a quota opportunity reproduced their local no-quota choices exactly, and paired behavior agreed through the first intervention in every session, narrowing the change to admission and the subsequent feedback it altered.

The result supports a tradeoff between early progress and later refinement. The parent obtained fifteen actual incumbent gains from repeated-core analogues, while the child gained only six incumbents from its locally added families. These are observations from separate completed trajectories, so they cannot price the child’s unscored rejected molecules or establish that those particular rejections caused the endpoint loss. The chemical assessment helps explain why counting cores is insufficient: productive attachment positions and combinations of peripheral groups remained uneven despite broader ring coverage. The number of evaluated molecules with potential tetrahedral centres rose from 846 to 1,145, with no assigned configurations in either cohort; the quota supplied neither configuration control nor a guarantee of preserving useful functional roles.

The open question is whether broader early coverage can coexist with sufficient sampling of productive peripheral analogues to retain late improvements. The AUC gain makes that distinction worth testing, while the lower final score rules out treating increased family coverage alone as evidence of better search.
finding_summary.results:
The admission mechanism executed correctly in all 497 sampling calls. It rejected 459 otherwise novel repeat-core draws before capacity and produced no repeated ring core within a call; the parent emitted 460 such repetitions. Against equal-sized choices from the same actual draws, 154 calls gained a total of 264 family slots: 259 ring-core appearances and five acyclic singleton appearances. Every added family reached evaluation, and six of those molecules improved the incumbent. Across complete runs, distinct evaluated ring cores increased from 2,813 to 3,079, while the largest occupancy of one core in a session fell from 160 molecules to 44. Total strict incumbent improvements nevertheless fell from 149 to 120.

The three-seed mean final score decreased from 0.522705 to 0.508379, a paired change of −0.014326 against the required +0.002 benefit. Seed changes were +0.002392, −0.018880 and −0.026492. All five task means declined, although the DRD2 endpoint difference was only about two millionths near the score ceiling. Recorded mean AUC increased from 0.405593 to 0.427858; about 94% of that aggregate increase came from DRD2, mainly its much earlier progress in seed 2. All fifteen sessions completed their budgets. Batches needing refills increased from 16 to 33, and measured generation time increased from 24.75 to 37.02 seconds. The utility falsifier is triggered; the verified admission mechanism remains confirmed.

finding_summary.headline: The quota broadened evaluated scaffold coverage but lowered final scores despite earlier progress.
finding_summary.insights:
This resolves the earlier uncertainty about whether protected alternatives ever reach useful downstream opportunities. Here, all 264 locally added families were scored, and 111 of their molecules entered fitting, making 212 training appearances, including 101 historical replay appearances. Direct admission therefore carried diversification through evaluation and learning. That propagation was insufficient for a final-score benefit. The 337 calls without a quota opportunity reproduced their local no-quota choices exactly, and paired behavior agreed through the first intervention in every session, narrowing the change to admission and the subsequent feedback it altered.

The result supports a tradeoff between early progress and later refinement. The parent obtained fifteen actual incumbent gains from repeated-core analogues, while the child gained only six incumbents from its locally added families. These are observations from separate completed trajectories, so they cannot price the child’s unscored rejected molecules or establish that those particular rejections caused the endpoint loss. The chemical assessment helps explain why counting cores is insufficient: productive attachment positions and combinations of peripheral groups remained uneven despite broader ring coverage. The number of evaluated molecules with potential tetrahedral centres rose from 846 to 1,145, with no assigned configurations in either cohort; the quota supplied neither configuration control nor a guarantee of preserving useful functional roles.

The open question is whether broader early coverage can coexist with sufficient sampling of productive peripheral analogues to retain late improvements. The AUC gain makes that distinction worth testing, while the lower final score rules out treating increased family coverage alone as evidence of better search.

finding_summary.headline: The quota broadened evaluated scaffold coverage but lowered final scores despite earlier progress.
finding_summary.insights:
This resolves the earlier uncertainty about whether protected alternatives ever reach useful downstream opportunities. Here, all 264 locally added families were scored, and 111 of their molecules entered fitting, making 212 training appearances, including 101 historical replay appearances. Direct admission therefore carried diversification through evaluation and learning. That propagation was insufficient for a final-score benefit. The 337 calls without a quota opportunity reproduced their local no-quota choices exactly, and paired behavior agreed through the first intervention in every session, narrowing the change to admission and the subsequent feedback it altered.

The result supports a tradeoff between early progress and later refinement. The parent obtained fifteen actual incumbent gains from repeated-core analogues, while the child gained only six incumbents from its locally added families. These are observations from separate completed trajectories, so they cannot price the child’s unscored rejected molecules or establish that those particular rejections caused the endpoint loss. The chemical assessment helps explain why counting cores is insufficient: productive attachment positions and combinations of peripheral groups remained uneven despite broader ring coverage. The number of evaluated molecules with potential tetrahedral centres rose from 846 to 1,145, with no assigned configurations in either cohort; the quota supplied neither configuration control nor a guarantee of preserving useful functional roles.

The open question is whether broader early coverage can coexist with sufficient sampling of productive peripheral analogues to retain late improvements. The AUC gain makes that distinction worth testing, while the lower final score rules out treating increased family coverage alone as evidence of better search.

molecular_assessment.headline: Broad, ring-rich medicinal chemistry; productive attachment patterns and stereochemical definition remain uneven.
molecular_assessment.overall_character: All five supplied tasks and all three seeds were read, including the Parent trajectories. Each task contains 900 evaluated records, of which 870 are optimizer proposals. Passive RDKit inspection of the 4,350 Child proposals finds 4,350 parseable, single-component molecules, 4,303 containing rings and 4,199 containing aromatic rings. The typical proposal has 26 heavy atoms and three perceived rings. The digest's ring-closure rates are 0.9828–0.9943 and aromatic-marker rates are 0.9391–0.992; these are fractions of SMILES containing markers, not fractions of atoms. Aromatic amides, sulfonamides, fused nitrogen heterocycles, arylpiperazines and arylpiperidines are well represented. Most recognizable small-molecule families are plausibly makeable, while the tails include simple inorganic species, oversized polyaromatics or peptides, and unusual nitrogen functionality. Drug-likeness is moderate because plausible medicinal frameworks coexist with substantial size, flexibility and substitution liabilities; no synthesis route or experimental property was established. Structural breadth is real: the evaluated proposals contain 3,079 distinct atom/bond-typed nonisomeric Murcko ring scaffolds versus 2,813 in the Parent. Functional roles and productive substitution patterns remain much more specific than these scaffold counts. RDKit identifies potential tetrahedral centres in 1,145 Child proposals, versus 846 Parent proposals, with zero assigned centres in either; all task digest stereocentre-marker rates are also zero. This is missing configuration coverage, not evidence that a particular stereoisomer would score better. Counts retain repeated identities across seeds. Reproducible passive descriptors, input hashes and recorded-score comparisons are saved in r0012-05-improve-L03-molecular.audit.py and r0012-05-improve-L03-molecular.audit.json beside this report.

per_task.generated_character: The 870 proposals have a median of 24 heavy atoms, three rings and three aromatic rings. They are chiefly aromatic amides: acetamido benzodiazines, benzimidazole-containing systems, lactams, benzylamides and diaryl ether carboxamides carrying amidines. The leading acetamido benzodiazine/phenethyl structures have 22 heavy atoms and three aromatic rings, with ordinary amide and carbon–carbon attachment chemistry that looks synthetically plausible. Other proposals extend into large peptides and densely fused polycycles. Evaluated ring-core diversity is 604 versus the Parent's 539, while the recognizable high-scoring chemical vocabulary remains aromatic carbonyl/nitrogen chemistry.
liabilities: Large peptide extensions and highly substituted polyaromatics impose much greater size or conformational burden than the leading compact amides; extra amide or ring content alone does not retain the observed score.
Amidines change ionization and hydrogen-bonding character relative to neutral aromatic amides. Their presence is not equivalent to retaining the same nitrogen functionality.
The saturated and polycyclic tail includes unresolved tetrahedral configurations: 178 proposals contain potential tetrahedral centres and none are assigned.
missing_features: Consistent assembly of the compact aromatic amide environment is missing from many proposals: heteroarenes and carbonyls are available, but the useful combination of size, attachment position and nitrogen role is often lost during elaboration.

The leading benzodiazine positional variants do not reveal a productive direction beyond their shared score. The stronger pyridyl ether/carboxamide combinations observed in the Parent are absent from the Child's leading examples.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial indole carboxanilide scores 0.3051048083696145; four acetamido benzodiazine positional variants reach the same 0.4428306005333078. The upper recorded-score quartile occupies 20–29 heavy atoms, whereas the lower quartile spans 1–49. A fluorine-only molecule scores 0.0 and the cited 44-heavy-atom peptide extension scores 6.353312339014414e-28. Among final proposals, the amidinoaryl pyrrolidine amide scores 0.3173316605218366, but adding another aryl carboxamide gives 0.0004762091843102436. These observations favor a bounded combination of aromatic extent, nitrogen placement and carbonyl attachment, rather than monotonic elaboration. The Parent's seed-2 pyridyl ether carboxanilide at evaluation 271 scores 0.5, whereas the Child's amidine-bearing diaryl ether example reaches 0.42749549733373915; the Child seed-0 best improves on the Parent's 0.43351949803907636. The chemistry changes are uneven across seeds, and the examples do not identify a unique missing target structure.

per_task.generated_character: The proposals are especially aromatic and halogen-rich: medians are 31 heavy atoms, four rings and four aromatic rings, and the digest halogen-marker rate is 0.8747. The leading family is methoxy-substituted anilino quinazoline chemistry with a phenyl, furyl or thienyl appendage and fluorinated aniline. The best example has 27 heavy atoms and four aromatic rings; its exocyclic NH, ring nitrogen acceptors and ether are recognizable, synthetically plausible medicinal chemistry. The full trajectories also contain hydrazone-rich and other nitrogen-heteroaromatic families, polyaryl ethers and sulfones. Observed ring cores number 505 versus 355 in the Parent, but all twelve digest-best entries remain close relatives of the anilino fused-diazine family.
liabilities: Extensive aromatic surface and repeated halogenation create a plausible solubility burden; neither adding fluorine nor adding more aromatic rings consistently improves the recorded score.
The lower tail includes an activated alkene flanked by sulfonyl and ester functionality, which deserves a different reactivity reading from the stable aromatic ether examples.
Simple inorganic or very small nitrogen-containing proposals are chemically valid species but poor evidence of useful molecular construction for this observed family.
missing_features: The strongest Child family lacks the coordinated alkoxy decoration of the stronger Parent example. The missing evidence concerns successful combinations and positions of appendages, rather than access to aromatic rings, fluorine or ether groups individually.

The digest-best set contains no comparably successful alternative arrangement of the anilino donor and heteroaromatic acceptors outside this close fused-diazine family. The observed gradient provides no basis for prescribing extra saturation or basic amines.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The difluoroanilino phenylquinazoline scores 0.6460611381594701, and its trifluoro analogue scores 0.6456917428325912. Furyl and thienyl replacements each score 0.6439546794971287; these substitutions mostly preserve the local plateau. A four-aromatic-ring polyaryl ether/methylsulfone scores only 0.30122048819527814, showing that aromatic ring count alone does not explain the ordering. The vinylsulfone/unsaturated-ester example scores 0.2948214550303749, while even nitrate receives 0.5004402958788305, so a middle-range numerical value does not establish a coherent organic framework. The Parent's seed-2 evaluation-273 best is a more extensively alkoxy-decorated anilino phenylquinazoline at 0.6669492630755185. The Child preserves the general core but does not reproduce that higher-scoring peripheral arrangement among its best molecules.

per_task.generated_character: The proposals combine saturated amine rings with aromatic groups: median size is 27 heavy atoms, with four rings and two aromatic rings. The leading 24-heavy-atom arylalkyl piperidine and 29-heavy-atom arylpiperazine contain a neutral, structurally basic aliphatic nitrogen connected to hydrophobic aromatic regions. Other strong examples combine piperazines or benzazepines with phenols, methoxy groups, aniline, fluorinated heteroarenes and flexible alkyl linkers. These simple cyclic-amine families look conventionally makeable. Seed-2 later proposals also explore fused and bridged phenolic polycycles with greater configurational complexity. The Parent already generated strong arylpiperazines, benzazepine-linked amines and amino ketones; cyclic basic nitrogen is established chemistry in both cohorts.
liabilities: Several near-ceiling molecules have long flexible linkers and substantial hydrophobic aromatic surface. Their recorded scores do not resolve conformational, solubility or selectivity liabilities.

The fused and bridged phenolic alternatives can contain multiple unresolved stereocentres, making their synthetic and conformational interpretation less definite than the simple piperidine or piperazine examples.
Sulfonylation, acylation and direct aromatic attachment change nitrogen basicity. A low charged-SMILES rate does not mean the high-scoring neutral representations lack protonatable amines.
missing_features: No absent objective-required ring or amine motif is demonstrated: the highest-scoring proposals already contain the strongly associated cyclic aliphatic nitrogen and aromatic groups.

Configurational definition is missing from the complex saturated alternatives. There are 420 proposals with potential tetrahedral centres and zero assigned centres; the present scores do not establish whether stereochemical control would improve this objective.

The quota resets on every existing raw sampling call and uses no task identity, score, accepted elite content, fitted chemistry cutoff or time-dependent rule. approach.method_basis: The Parent trains a recurrent SMILES language model on an unlabeled molecular corpus and starts each objective with a fresh policy copied from that frozen prior. Each accepted batch supplies its highest-scoring half, joined by the strongest eligible earlier elites from a memory of thirty-two accepted molecules. Historical examples keep their original strings and scores and receive diminishing weights according to earlier fitting exposure, with the total current and historical coefficient shares preserved. The policy fits squared error toward frozen-prior sequence log likelihood plus sixty times accepted reward, with each positive target independently capped at zero. It takes the inherited clipped Adam updates and retains the final policy. Complete SMILES are then sampled directly from that policy, and the first chemically valid, canonically novel draws fill the announced batch. Extra valid novel draws from those same calls are discarded.
approach.novelty: Add a quota of one emitted molecule per ring scaffold within each existing sampling call. The first eligible member of a scaffold is admitted in sample order; later members in that call are skipped. A refill starts a fresh allowance, so a productive scaffold can still contribute again without a global diversity ban. This moves core allocation to the point where freshly generated molecules actually reach evaluation. The earlier sibling diversified retained historical memory, where most protected alternatives never reached a later fitting update and the mean gain missed the meaningful threshold. Other siblings changed the prior or learning rule. None tested a quota on the direct emitted stream. This experiment keeps the current strong replay and target-ceiling stack and measures which sampled core alternatives gain emission. The Parent also improved through peripheral analogues, so losing productive local substitutions is a concrete risk; more core names alone will not establish useful search.

research_intent.falsifier: The admission mechanism is refuted if two successfully extracted identical nonempty ring-scaffold keys are emitted in one generation call, if a later eligible occurrence before capacity is admitted despite an earlier same-key emission, if a first eligible core is rejected solely by this quota, or if the allowance persists into the next call. Grouping all acyclic molecules together, changing canonical/isomeric identity, emitting a saved or edited molecule, or introducing an unrelated chemical or score threshold violates the bound mechanism. If repeat-core opportunities occur but neither actual emitted identities nor conditional equal-count family coverage changes on any qualifying call, the claim that the gate moves emitted support is unsupported; no opportunities leaves it untested. A core extraction failure must follow the declared original-admission fallback and be counted rather than hidden. The first-k same-draw comparator must use identical initial exclusions and recorded raw draws without extra randomness or labels. Inconsistent novelty accounting, changed learned weights on identical feedback, altered upstream memory/loss rules or unbounded refill violates isolation. Increased core coverage with a paired mean benefit below the supplied threshold, or incomplete generation that prevents a complete paired comparison, rejects utility without undoing verified quota activation. Loss of productive analogues, unchanged session-wide core counts and repeats across separate refill calls do not themselves refute the call-local mechanism.
